name: Non-polyposis Turcot Syndrome
aliases: Hereditary Colorectal Cancer with Brain Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of colorectal adenocarcinoma without multiple polyposis
Presence of primary brain tumor, typically glioblastoma multiforme or medulloblastoma
Family history of Lynch syndrome-associated cancers or Turcot syndrome
Evidence of mismatch repair gene mutations (e.g., MLH1, MSH2) or microsatellite instability

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of colorectal adenocarcinoma without polyposis plus a primary brain tumor, supported by genetic evidence of mismatch repair deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of clinical, pathological, and genetic findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Primary malignant brain tumor (glioblastoma multiforme or medulloblastoma)

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain related to colorectal tumor
searchTerms: abdominal discomfort related to bowel cancer
belly pain due to colorectal tumor
low blood count from gut bleeding
anemia due to digestive tract bleeding

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances from brain tumor mass effect
searchTerms: vision problems from brain tumor pressure
eye disturbances due to brain mass

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to intracranial pressure
searchTerms: feeling sick due to intracranial pressure

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to brain tumor obstruction
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

laboratory: Immunohistochemistry showing loss of mismatch repair proteins (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2)
imaging: MRI or CT showing primary brain tumors (glioblastoma multiforme or medulloblastoma)
Colonoscopy revealing colorectal adenocarcinoma without multiple polyps
genetic: Germline mutations in mismatch repair genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2)
other: Family history consistent with Lynch syndrome or Turcot syndrome
Histopathology confirming colorectal adenocarcinoma and brain tumor subtype

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple colorectal adenomatous polyps
APC gene mutations instead of mismatch repair gene mutations
Family history of colorectal and endometrial cancers

redFlags: Primary malignant brain tumor in young patient
Family history of Lynch syndrome-associated cancers
references: Lynch HT, de la Chapelle A. Hereditary colorectal cancer. N Engl J Med. 2003 Mar 6;348(10):919-32.
Turcot syndrome: clinical features and molecular genetics. J Med Genet. 1995;32(12):1003-7.
